models_evaluated: polar map-free 3D deep learning MPI model (in-house)

links.outcome: Performance drop of AI model between development-site and external-site cohorts
links.effect: External cohort AUC lower than internal: patient-based 0.713 vs. 0.813; vessel-based 0.733 vs. 0.782.
links.quote: The model showed significantly lower performance in the external cohort compared to the internal cohort in both patient-based (AUC: 0.713 vs. 0.813) and vessel-based (AUC: 0.733 vs. 0.782) analyses, but still outperformed stress TPD (all p < 0.001).

links.effect: Model performance was significantly lower at the external site than the internal site (patient AUC 0.713 vs 0.813).
links.quote: The model showed significantly lower performance in the external cohort compared to the internal cohort in both patient-based (AUC: 0.713 vs. 0.813) and vessel-based (AUC: 0.733 vs. 0.782) analyses, but still outperformed stress TPD (all p < 0.001).

links.outcome: AI performance differences across patient subgroups (stress type, age)
links.effect: Performance lower in treadmill stress MPI patients in the internal cohort and in patients over 70 years old in the external cohort.
links.quote: The performance was lower in patients who underwent treadmill stress MPI in the internal cohort and in patients over 70 years old in the external cohort.

links.outcome: AI model compared with conventional stress TPD on same data
links.effect: The DL model outperformed stress TPD in both internal and external cohorts (all p < 0.001), despite lower external performance.

screen.reason: The study conducts an external validation of a deep learning model for myocardial perfusion imaging across two institutions to assess generalizability and demographic bias, but it evaluates diagnostic performance retrospectively without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
